title: Traffic Sheriff: Statistical Watchdog and Adaptive Abort for Model Version Experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, policy-driven Statistical Watchdog service (aka 'Traffic Sheriff') that monitors live model version experiments (canaries, A/B tests, shadow traffic) and performs automated mitigation when statistical checks show degradation or instability. The service will integrate with rollout controller, routing layer, and Console to provide visibility and control.

Why: Current rollout tooling surfaces exposure controls but lacks continuous, statistically sound automatic aborts for multi-metric regressions and stateful instability (e.g., KV cache mismatch, latency spikes correlated with certain sequences). We want safe automated rollback for high-risk production experiments while giving product owners granular tolerances.

Scope:
- Experiment lifecycle hooks: start, pause, resume, abort, finalize.
- Continuous statistical inference: sequential testing (alpha-spending), Bayesian credible intervals, and CUSUM-like drift detection.
- Multi-metric composite scoring (primary metric + safety metrics) and configurable abort policies.
- Shadow traffic-aware checks that validate correctness metrics without affecting user experience.
- Integration points: rollout controller (can trigger rollback), routing layer (change exposure), Console (UI for policies and live telemetry), and alerts (PagerDuty/Slack).
- API for programmatic policy creation and a default safe policy for common use cases.

Non-goals: deep offline A/B analysis tooling, experiment visualization beyond key telemetry, and replacing the evaluation framework used by Research for offline ground-truth tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Watchdog can attach to an experiment and evaluate a configurable primary metric at user-defined cadence (default 1 minute).
2) Support at least three statistical strategies selectable per experiment: sequential p-value with alpha spending, Bayesian credible interval thresholding, and drift detector (CUSUM).
3) Automatic abort action is performed when policy conditions are met; abort is recorded and annotated in experiment history and Console with reason and supporting stats.

4) Shadow traffic experiments are supported: correctness metrics computed on shadowed requests and surfaced, and shadow failures do not impact user-facing routing unless policy explicitly allows failover.

5) Console exposes a compact policy editor with presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and a preview of historical false-positive rate based on simulation using stored historical traffic samples.
6) Webhooks/alerts are emitted for near-threshold conditions (warning) and aborts (critical).

7) End-to-end test: run a synthetic canary that introduces a 5% drop in primary metric and verify automated rollback within the policy SLO for conservative preset in <= 30 minutes under normal traffic patterns.
implementation_notes: We will implement the Watchdog as a separate service to keep lifecycle logic independent of the routing plane; it will subscribe to telemetry via streaming Kafka topic and maintain lightweight state per experiment.
Statistical strategies: start with Wald's SPRT-like alpha spending for quick detection, and add a Bayesian option for low-traffic experiments where credible intervals are more stable.
To avoid noisy aborts, policies include a minimum sample requirement and cool-down windows; default conservative preset sets min samples=1000 and alpha=0.01.

Auto-rollback flow: Watchdog issues Abort command to Rollout Controller API which transitions experiment to 'rolled back' and flips routing rules; rollback must be idempotent and reversible by human override.
Telemetry: persist summary stats per minute to the metrics store to allow retrospective analysis and simulation. Include sample size, effect size, p-value/credible interval, and drift score.
Privacy and security: no raw customer content will be persisted by Watchdog; only hashed keys and aggregated metrics will be stored. Coordinate with Security for final sign-off.
steps: 1) Finalize policy model and presets with SRE and Research (week 1).
2) Implement Watchdog service skeleton and streaming ingestion (week 2-3).
3) Add sequential testing and Bayesian modules; unit tests and statistical sims (week 3-4).
4) Rollout controller integration and abort flow; QA on staging (week 5).
5) Console UI for policy editor and incident annotations (week 6).
6) Canary rollout to internal teams and evaluate false-positive/negative rates, tune defaults (week 7-8).
